name: sau_ent
description: S. aureus enterotoxin gene panel: SEA-SEE, SEG-SEY, SEl26-28, SEl30-33, SElV/X/Z, SEU, SEO, SElU2 and TSST-1 + the nuc species control, with variant alleles for SEC, SEI, SEN, SEU and TSST-1
note: Twenty-five enterotoxin, enterotoxin-like and TSST-1 references converted from the indexofire/enterotoxin abricate database (commit 30c022eeb712, 2023-08-27; MIT). Sequences are the upstream records byte-for-byte; only the headers are rewritten to gspec/v1 and a curated product string is attached per gene. Fourteen curated additions cut from public-domain INSDC records (each committed as a build asset whose FASTA header carries the citation): seu from AY205305 (Letertre 2003; implicated in outbreaks without classical SEs, Umeda 2017), SElU2 from EF030428 (Thomas 2006; widely called SElW after Collery & Smyth 2007 — the 2026 review restores SElU2 because the 2012 'true SElW' is a different, non-emetic protein), seo from AF285760:370-1155 (Jarraud 2001, the original egc cluster deposit; a gap the Fanelli 2022 backtest exposed), the SEC3 allele from X51661 (Hovde 1990), the SEC-bovine and TSST-1 bovine-SaPI alleles from AF217235 (Fitzgerald 2001), the egc3 variant alleles for sei/seu/sen from AY158703 (96.7-97.7 % to prototypes; Letertre), SEl28 from MN450304:2472-3197 (egc SaPI of strain 364P, Fanelli deposit), SEl30 from PZ361155, and sel31/sel32/sel33 from AFTU01000025.1 and FGMI01000018.1 (Dicks 2021, each verified 100 % aa-identical to Table S3). NOMENCLATURE AUDIT: the upstream gene labels sel26/sel27 (MF370874, 744/753 bp) follow the primary designation paper (Zhang et al., IJMM 2018: 'designated SEl26 and SEl27') and the 2026 nomenclature-clarification review (Franjus et al.: SEl26-1 744 nt, SEl27-1 753 nt, SEl28 = SEl26-2 726 nt); the conflicting sel27/sel28 numbering in the MF370874/78 description lines and MN450304's CDS labels follows no peer-reviewed paper and is not adopted. REMAINING GAPS (deliberate, documented in scripts/staphylococcus/README.md): SEC2 (no complete INSDC record; SEC1 covers at 97.4 % protein identity), sel29p (pseudogene, absent from contemporary strains), SE01/SE02 (Suzuki 2020, accessions behind paywalled full text), sel34/sel35 (bioRxiv preprint, unreviewed), and the remaining variant alleles for seg/sek/sem/sey (Lefebvre 2022 inventory). Variant alleles share the parent gene id and are distinguished by the accession. One species control added, staphylococcal thermonuclease (nuc) from public-domain INSDC NC_007795.1:800034-800720. Screen-only; no typing scheme. If any author or rights holder objects to the use or redistribution of this database, please contact indexofire@gmail.com and the content will be removed or adjusted promptly upon verification.

references.citation: Argudin MA, Mendoza MC, Rodicio MR. Food poisoning and Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxins. Toxins (Basel). 2010;2(7):1751-1773.
references.note: The SE/SEl gene family and its nomenclature.

references.citation: Lefebvre D, Blanco-Valle K, Hennekinne JA, Simon S, Fenaille F, Becher F, Nia Y. Multiplex detection of 24 staphylococcal enterotoxins in culture supernatant using liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry. Toxins (Basel). 2022;14(4):249.
references.note: The variant inventory per gene (sec 10, seu 10, sem 9, sen 9, sek 8, seg 6, sey 6, tsst1 6) this panel's variant alleles mitigate.

caveats: Gene presence is toxigenic potential, not toxin production: expression is strain-, niche- and growth-dependent. Food or isolate enterotoxin positivity still needs an immunological assay (ELISA) or expression evidence.

The 'enterotoxin-like' types (SEl26, SEl27, SElV, SElW, SElX, SElZ) are grouped by sequence homology; emetic activity is not demonstrated for all of them, so reporting them as enterotoxins overstates the risk.

Sequence polymorphism is the family norm (Lefebvre et al. 2022: six to ten variants per gene for sec, seg, sek, sem, sen, seu, sey and tsst1). This panel carries variant alleles for sec, sei, sen, seu and tsst1; other genes remain one reference per type, and divergence beyond these alleles can still fall below the default floors (80 % identity / 80 % coverage) — key on identity and coverage, not presence alone.

nuc is the species control: its absence argues against S. aureus (or a failed screen), while the toxin panel alone does not establish the species. S. argenteus carries SElZ-like genes — key on the accession, not the gene name alone.
Upstream references are single per-type accessions from varied strains; alleles can diverge below the default screen floors (80 % identity / 80 % coverage).
